text: . The festival of Chhath Puja is being observed with religious fervour and devotion across the country, particularly in Bihar, Jharkhand, eastern Uttar Pradesh and Delhi. On the second day of the four-day festival, devotees will be observing the traditional Kharna ritual today.On the occasion, devotees observe a day-long fast, abstaining from both food and water. The fast is broken in the evening after offering prayers to the Sun God and Chhathi Maiya. As part of the rituals, traditional prasad, including jaggery-based kheer and wheat rotis, is prepared with great devotion. The offerings are first presented to the deities, following which devotees consume the prasad and distribute it among family members.Kharna holds special significance as it marks the beginning of the rigorous 36-hour Nirjala Vrat. After performing the evening rituals and consuming the Kharna prasad, devotees embark on this strict fast, abstaining from both food and water. The fast continues until the concluding rituals of the festival. The four-day festival began yesterday with the traditional Nahay-Khay ritual.Tomorrow, on the third day, devotees will gather along riverbanks, ponds and other water bodies to offer prayers and Arghya to the setting Sun. This ritual is known as Sandhya Arghya. The festival will conclude on Monday morning with Usha Arghya, when devotees will offer prayers and water to the rising Sun. This marks the final ritual of Chhath Puja, following which devotees break their nearly 36-hour-long fast.Dedicated to the worship of the Sun God and Chhathi Maiya, Chhath Puja is among the most significant festivals in Bihar and neighbouring regions. The festival embodies devotion, discipline and gratitude towards nature and the Sun, regarded as the ultimate source of energy and life.

. Niraj Kumar today won the bronze medal in the men’s 50m rifle three-positions event at the World Shooting Championships in Doha. Niraj has also secured a quota place for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.This marks India’s second Olympic quota from the championships. Previously, Jaypal Malviya had secured the first quota by winning a silver medal in the men’s 10m air pistol event.

. Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment Dr Virendra Kumar today inaugurated the Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 at Dilli Haat, INA in New Delhi this evening. The Mela will provide a dedicated marketing platform to artisans and beneficiaries belonging to Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes, Safai Karamcharis and persons with disabilities to showcase and market their products to a wider audience. Speaking on the occassion, Dr Kumar said the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment has been organising Shilp Samagam Melas since 2022 and more than 1,000 artisans from Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes and Safai Karamcharis have benefited from opportunities to exhibit and market their products.  The Minister said that with approximately 150 stalls for participating male and female artisans to showcase their handicraft and handloom products under Bharat TULIP and Purple Fest, the initiative brings traditional artisans, creative talent and persons with disabilities together on a common platform to encourage wider market access and equal opportunities for participation.  The Mela will remain open to visitors until 15th of this month.

. The Baloch American Congress (BAC) has appealed to international investors, world leaders and the United Nations to ensure that Balochistan’s natural resources are not exploited through agreements with Pakistani authorities without the meaningful consent of the Baloch people.In a formal letter addressed to the United Nations, world leaders and international investors, Dr Tara Chand Baloch, President of the Baloch American Congress, urged the international community to respect the rights of the Baloch people and recognise their role in deciding the future of their land and natural resources. Balochistan possesses significant natural wealth, including gold, copper, valuable minerals and a strategic coastline. However, Dr Tara Chand alleged that despite these resources, the local population continues to face poverty, unemployment and a lack of basic facilities. The letter also cited the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) as a warning to international investors, arguing that projects pursued without the consent of the Baloch people have contributed to resistance and serious setbacks. The BAC president also called upon the United Nations and governments across the world to support the human rights, freedom and peaceful self-determination of the Baloch people, including their aspirations for independence.Meanwhile, Shafi Burfat, Chairman of the Jeay Sindh Muttahida Mahaz, JSMM, has accused Pakistan’s military establishment of exploiting the natural resources and political rights of Sindh, Balochistan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and other historic nations to sustain its political and economic dominance.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi today paid tributes to former Prime Minister Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru on his birth anniversary. Pandit Nehru was born on this day in the year 1889 at Anand Bhawan in Prayagraj.Defence Minister Rajnath Singh paid tributes to former Prime Minister Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru on his birth anniversary today. In a social media post, Mr Singh said, Pandit Nehru’s contribution to India’s freedom struggle and his leadership as the first Prime Minister of independent India left a enduring imprint on the formative years of the nation.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said India is moving towards global leadership in emerging technologies, from chips to ships, and from Artificial Intelligence and data centres to quantum computing. He emphasised that reliable power generation is essential to achieving this ambition. Mr Modi said the country is expanding its nuclear power capacity as part of its efforts to achieve clean energy goals and meet its growing energy requirements.The Prime Minister was addressing the gathering at Bengaluru in Karnataka yesterday, after launching development projects worth over 15,600 crore rupees. Mr Modi said the projects, covering metro, railways and energy infrastructure, will strengthen connectivity, boost economic growth and create new employment opportunities in the state.Prime Minister Modi highlighted the importance of energy security in view of the ongoing conflict in the Iran and Gulf region. He said India strengthened its energy infrastructure over the past decade by expanding fuel production and storage capacity, along with investments in solar, hydro and wind energy. He said India’s renewable energy capacity had crossed 300 gigawatts. Pointing out that Central schemes are transforming Indian citizens from electricity consumers into electricity producers, he also highlighted the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana and PM-KUSUM scheme, saying these initiatives are helping households and farmers become producers of clean energy.The Prime Minister also outlined three major energy projects in Karnataka. These include the Mangaluru LPG project, which will add 80,000 metric tonnes of storage capacity; the Devangonthi Marketing Terminal, aimed at streamlining the supply of petrol, diesel and aviation fuel; and a compressed biogas plant in Bengaluru, with a production capacity of 13 tonnes per day. Mr Modi said the biogas plant will improve waste management and help reduce expenditure on natural gas imports.Describing Bengaluru as India’s Silicon Valley, Prime Minister Modi said the city contributes more than one-third of the country’s IT exports and serves as a major centre of innovation and economic growth. He noted that the Namma Metro network has expanded from just 17 kilometres in 2014 to over 100 kilometres today, making Bengaluru the third city in the country, after Delhi-NCR and the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, to achieve this milestone. He said the newly inaugurated Pink Line of Bengaluru Metro will improve connectivity to educational institutions, including IIM Bengaluru, as well as major business and technology hubs.The Prime Minister also highlighted railway modernisation, including the development of Amrit Bharat stations and the expansion of Vande Bharat services. He also flagged off a new Vande Bharat train connecting Karnataka with Goa, following the recent introduction of the state’s first Vande Bharat Sleeper train. He said the new service would improve connectivity along Karnataka’s coastal region, including Mangaluru, and offer passengers a faster and more comfortable travel experience.

. Indian women’s hockey player and Olympian Lalremsiami Hmar today became the first sportsperson from Mizoram to receive the prestigious Arjuna Award, adding another milestone to her trailblazing career.The 26-year-old was among 17 sportspersons selected for the Arjuna Award 2025 by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports on August 18. President Droupadi Murmu formally presented the honour to her at a ceremony at Rashtrapati Bhavan in New Delhi today.Lalremsiami, who hailed from Kolasib in the northern part of Mizoram bordering Assam, took up hockey at a young age.Her talent was spotted by teachers Lallawmawmi, Lalrampari and Lalrothuami, who encouraged her to pursue the sport.Lalremsiami joined the state-run hockey academy at Thenzawl in 2011 at the age of 11, before moving to the National Hockey Academy in New Delhi in 2016.Lalremsiami made her national debut at the Junior Nehru Hockey Tournament in October 2011 and was later selected for India’s Under-18 team for the Asian Cup in 2016.She earned her first senior national team call-up in 2017 and was part of India’s Asia Cup-winning side that year.Since then, she has established herself as a key member of the Indian team, featuring in several major international tournaments, including the Tokyo Olympics 2020, where India finished fourth.She created history in 2018 by becoming the first sportsperson from Mizoram to win an Asian Games medal, helping India secure silver.Her commitment to the national team drew widespread admiration in 2019 when she chose to remain with the squad for the FIH Women’s Series in Japan despite the death of her father, Lalthansanga Zote.India won the tournament and secured qualification for the Tokyo Olympics, making Lalremsiami the first woman from Mizoram to compete at the Olympics.She followed in the footsteps of archer C. Lalremsanga, who represented India at the 1992 Barcelona and 1996 Atlanta Olympics.In 2020, Lalremsiami became the first Indian female hockey player to win the International Hockey Federation’s Women’s Rising Star of the Year award.Her list of achievements has since grown to include a bronze at the 2022 Asian Games, Asian Champions Trophy titles in 2023 and 2024, and gold at the 2026 Asian Games.The Mizoram government had earlier announced a cash reward of Rs 40 lakh each for Lalremsiami and fellow Mizo player Lalthantluangi for their contribution to India’s women’s hockey team that won gold at the Asian Games on October 2.The Arjuna Award now adds another distinction to Lalremsiami’s career, making her the first sportsperson from Mizoram to receive one of the country’s highest honours for sporting achievement.

. Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claimed that its forces targeted and destroyed a US early-warning radar system in Bahrain. In a statement carried by Iranian state broadcaster today, the IRGC reportedly said it had had targeted the radar system on the island of Bahrain in retaliation for what it described as an enemy air attack on a telecommunications tower in Sirik, a port city in southern Iran. IRGC also described the strike as a warning to the United States to stop its aerial operations and what it termed oil smuggling in the Strait of Hormuz.However, US Military’s Central Command (CENTCOM) disputed the Iranian claim, saying that the IRGC had launched two one-way attack drones towards Bahrain, both of which were intercepted by US forces. In an X post addressing the claim, CENTCOM said there were no injuries or damage.The conflict since February has seen Iran targeting US military installations across the Gulf. The latest claim, however, marks first such attack on US assets in a Gulf country in almost 2 months.

. The 45th Indian International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 will begin tomorrow at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. Talking to media, Chairman of India Trade Promotion Organisation, Jawed Ashraf said that this year the focus is on three key aspects that are enhancing the visitor experience, showcasing innovations and highlighting India’s rich heritage. He said that visitors can book tickets online through the IITF 2026 mobile application, which is integrated with the DMRC’s Sarthi app. Mr Ashraf informed that shuttle bus services will operate from several metro stations, including Mandi House, connecting visitors to all entry gates of the venue. Visitors can also reach Bharat Mandapam through app-based taxis, private vehicles and public transport. He added that parking facilities for around three thousand vehicles have been arranged, along with designated waiting areas for app-based taxis. Special facilities, including wheelchair assistance will also be available for senior citizens to ensure a comfortable and convenient experience.

. The nationwide ‘Viksit Bharat Yuva Samvad: Know Your Vote’ campaign has concluded with 536 Yuva Samvads conducted across 31 States and Union Territories. The campaign organised by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports through Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat) reached over one lakh young people and involved more than 5000 Youth Icons. The campaign brought discussions on electoral awareness to colleges and educational institutions across the country. It encouraged young people, particularly first-time voters, to understand their voting rights and electoral procedures and participate responsibly in democracy.The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports said that the campaign witnessed participation by Governors, Union Ministers, State Ministers, Members of Parliament and other public representatives. It added that sports personalities and youth icons from the sporting community also participated in programmes, sharing their experiences and encouraging youth participation in sports.The Yuva Samvads provided young participants with opportunities to seek clarity on electoral procedures, discuss voting rights and civic responsibilities, and interact directly with public representatives and Youth Icons.

. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has issued consolidated directions on domestic money transfers, retaining existing transaction limits while tightening safeguards for cash-based remittances. Individuals without bank accounts can remit funds up to Rs 50,000 to the bank account of a beneficiary through NEFT at bank branches.For transfers through business correspondents, ATMs and other permitted channels, the limit is Rs 5,000 per transaction and Rs 25,000 per remitter per month. Cash payouts to beneficiaries without bank accounts are capped at Rs 10,000 per transaction and Rs 25,000 per beneficiary per month.The RBI has retained mandatory remitter registration through a verified mobile number and self-certified valid document under KYC norms. Banks must include remitter details and cash-transfer identifiers in IMPS/NEFT messages, introduce transaction checks and customer alerts, investigate unusual credit patterns and report suspicious transactions. Transfers must be real-time or near real-time, with inter-bank settlements through RBI-approved systems. The directions cover banks, authorised payment operators and participants, while excluding card-to-card transfers.

. Union Minister of Home Affairs and Cooperation Amit Shah will be on a two-day visit to Pune starting tomorrow. He will attend the Bhoomi Pujan ceremony of the NHEC Multi-State Cooperative Society, virtually inaugurate the Regional Office of the Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies and launch Bharat Taxi at the NHEC Plant in Talegaon Dabhade tomorrow afternoon.On Monday morning, Mr Shah will visit the headquarters of Bharatiya Jain Sangathan and Shantilal Mutha Foundation on Senapati Bapat Marg in Pune. Later, he will unveil the statue of late Ajit Pawar at the Zilla Parishad Office, Yashwantrao Chavan Bhavan, on Wellesley Road in Pune.

. In the forex market today, the rupee depreciated by 21 paise to trade at Rs 94. 25 against the US dollar.The dollar index, which indicates US dollar’s strength against a basket of six other leading currencies, was trading at 103.23 in intra-day trade.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi reached Ahmedabad in Gujarat from Karnataka’s Mysuru last evening. He was received at the airport by Gujarat Governor Acharya Devvrat and Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel. The Prime Minister subsequently reached Gandhinagar, where he stayed overnight at Lok Bhavan.Welcoming the Prime Minister, Governor Devvrat praised his leadership and commitment to national development. He said Mr Modi’s vision of building a developed and self-reliant India by 2047 continued to inspire people across the country. Mr. Devvrat, in a social media post, said that under the guidance of the Prime Minister, Gujarat has emerged as a growth engine of the country’s development. He added that the state has set new benchmarks in natural farming, industrial growth and public welfare.Meanwhile, the Prime Minister’s scheduled visit to the Ambaji Temple in Banaskantha district today, on the occasion of Labh Pancham, which marks the culmination of Diwali celebrations in Gujarat, has been postponed in view of the large number of devotees visiting the shrine during the festive season.According to state authorities, more than 2.5 lakh devotees are visiting the temple every day, and the number is expected to cross five lakh today. Deputy Chief Minister Harsh Sanghavi said, the decision to reschedule the visit was taken to ensure that devotees do not face inconvenience due to security arrangements for the Prime Minister.The Ambaji temple is one of the 51 revered Shakti Peeths and attracts devotees from Gujarat and neighbouring states, particularly during the festive season.Gujarat Assembly Speaker Shankarbhai Chaudhary thanked the Prime Minister for giving priority to the convenience of devotees.

. India today defeated Maldives 1-0 in SAFF Championship Group B match at the National Stadium in Dhaka. Suhail Ahmad Bhat scored the match’s lone goal from the penalty spot in the 38th minute. With this the Blue Tigers entered the semi-finals.It was India’s second and final group match of the South Asian Football Federation (SAFF) Championships.India beat Pakistan 3-2 in their opening Group B match on 5th of this month.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices ended in negative zone today, snapping their three-day winning streak. The Sensex lost 319 points or 0.4 per cent to close at 81,592. The Nifty declined 155 points or 0.6 per cent to settle at 25,144. In the broader market on the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index fell over 0.2 per cent and the Smallcap 100 index shed 0.3 per cent.In the Sensex pack, 23 out of 30 constituent companies logged losses. Among the top underperformers, Mahindra and Mahindra shed over 2.1 per cent, Ultratech Cement lost 1.7 per cent and Bharat Electronics fell 1.6 per cent. In contrast, Hindustan Unilever rose 1.2 per cent, Asian Paints gained 0.9 per cent and Bharti Airtel added 0.7 per cent.In the sectoral indices on the BSE, 24 out of 28 sectors edged downwards. Among the top laggards, Realty dropped 1.7 per cent, Auto declined 1.2 per cent and Commodities shed 1.1 per cent.In contrast, Capital Goods gained 0.7 per cent, Power added over 0.3 per cent and Telecommunication rose 0.3 per cent.The overall market breadth at the BSE was negative, as shares of 2,462 companies declined, 1,965 advanced and 245 remained unchanged.

. Akashvani will broadcast the recording of the annual Sardar Patel Memorial Lecture, delivered by Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan, tonight at 9:30 PM. The recording will be broadcast across the entire Akashvani network on the occasion of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel’s birth anniversary.Delivering the 67th Sardar Patel Memorial Lecture, Mr Chouhan said that Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel’s vision, determination and leadership laid the foundation for India’s national unity and territorial integrity. He said that Sardar Patel’s efforts to integrate 565 princely states remain a defining chapter in the country’s history. The Minister emphasised that Patel’s vision of a united India continues to inspire the nation through the spirit of ‘Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat’.Mr Chouhan also said that, inspired by Sardar Patel’s firm approach towards national security and his policy of zero tolerance towards terrorism, India has responded decisively to threats from across its borders, including through measures such as surgical strikes.As a tribute to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, who served as independent India’s first Deputy Prime Minister and Information and Broadcasting Minister, Akashvani has been organising the annual Sardar Patel Memorial Lecture since 1955. Over the years, the annual event has served as a rich repository of thoughts, ideas and perspectives on a wide range of subjects. It has also provided an opportunity to gain a deeper understanding of India’s diverse cultural heritage and the various dimensions of its developmental challenges.

. Indian Railways has geared up to manage the ongoing festive season rush of Diwali and Chhath Puja, with extensive crowd management preparations underway at several railway stations. Ministry of Railways said that Indian Railways is developing dedicated passenger holding areas, known as Yatri Suvidha Kendras, at major railway stations across the country. This is being done to streamline passenger movement and ease congestion during periods of heavy footfall, including the festive season. The Yatri Suvidha Kendras, or Passenger Holding Areas, are being developed to provide dedicated space for unticketed and waiting passengers. Our correspondent reports that the facilities have been designed to ensure orderly passenger movement and provide a comfortable waiting environment.The holding areas have been designed to accommodate passengers before they proceed to the platform area. Talking to Akashvani News, Northern Railway CPRO  said that at New Delhi Railway station, a holding area is available for both reserved and unreserved classes. He said additional RPF personnel have also been deployed at Railway stations to facilitate passengers.At Anand Vihar Terminal, the Yatri Suvidha Kendra has 14 ticket counters, 16 CCTV cameras, four electronic display boards and seating for 20 passengers. The facility also has separate toilet facilities for male and female passengers, a Divyangjan toilet, an RO plant, 11 HVLS fans and a public announcement system. The aim is to reduce congestion on platforms, in circulating areas and at station approaches by providing designated spaces for waiting and ticketing.

. A 170-member Indian Defence Forces contingent departed today for Sri Lanka to participate in the 12th edition of India-Sri Lanka joint military exercise MITRA SHAKTI 2026. The exercise is scheduled to be conducted at the Army Training School, Maduru Oya, from today till 26th of this month. Defence Ministry said that the Indian contingent is drawn mainly from a battalion of the Rajputana Rifles, along with troops from other arms and services, and personnel from the Indian Air Force. The 14 day exercise aims to enhance joint military capability of both armies to undertake Counter Terrorism operations in a semi-urban environment under a United Nations mandate. It will focus on enhancing physical fitness, refining tactical drills and improving coordination between the participating contingents.Exercise ‘MITRA SHAKTI’ is an annual bilateral military exercise conducted alternately in India and Sri Lanka which provides an important platform for both armies to strengthen interoperability, exchange operational experiences and share best practices in the conduct of Counter Terrorism operations.

. In Badminton, Lakshya Sen progressed to the semifinals of the BWF Kumamoto Japan Masters after registering a comfortable straight-games victory over Yushi Tanaka in the quarterfinals. Lakshya defeated Tanaka of Japan 21-16, 21-15 to seal his place in the last four of the tournament. The Indian shuttler will next face Indonesia’s sixth seed Alwi Farhan in the semifinals tomorrow. Lakshya will look to overcome his previous record against Farhan, having lost both their earlier encounters.Meanwhile, Kidambi Srikanth bowed out of the tournament after suffering a straight-games defeat against Japan’s Koki Watanabe in the quarterfinals. Srikanth went down 22-24, 15-21 in a closely contested opening game before Watanabe secured the second game to seal his place in the semifinals.

. The depression, a remnant of Cyclone Arnab, over south Chhattisgarh and adjoining south Odisha has moved northwards.It is now centred over central Chhattisgarh and adjoining Odisha. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) said it is likely to move further north and weaken into a well-marked low-pressure area over north Chhattisgarh tonight.Meanwhile, IMD has issued a red alert for very heavy to extremely heavy rainfall in Bihar tomorrow.An orange alert has been issued for very heavy rainfall in East Uttar Pradesh, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal, Sikkim and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands tomorrow. Heavy rainfall is also expected in Jharkhand and Uttarakhand.Thunderstorms accompanied by hail are likely over East Rajasthan, Haryana, Chandigarh, Uttarakhand and West Uttar Pradesh.Thunderstorms and gusty winds are also forecast in several other states, including Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Punjab, Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Assam and Meghalaya.Meanwhile Delhi witnessed light to moderate rainfall this evening. The IMD has forecast very light rain accompanied by thunderstorms and lightning tomorrow morning.The maximum temperature is expected to remain between 26 and 28 degrees Celsius, while the minimum temperature is likely to range from 16 to 18 degrees Celsius.

. The US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) today temporarily halted departing flights across the country following a telecommunications failure that affected air traffic control centres, disrupting thousands of flights across the country.According to flight-tracking services, nearly 7,000 flights were delayed or cancelled following the ground stop. The FAA said the communications outage affected all 22 Air Route Traffic Control Centres across the United States, prompting the suspension of departures as a precautionary measure.Later, the US authorities lifted the nationwide ground stop that disrupted thousands of flights and stranded passengers across the country, clearing the way for airlines to resume operations after more than four hours.Meanwhile, US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said, FAA technicians are investigating the communications failure. Aircraft already in the air were allowed to land, while departing flights were temporarily suspended.The disruption initially affected air traffic control operations in Chicago before the FAA extended the restrictions nationwide.US Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there was no indication that the incident was linked to a security threat or deliberate attack. He assured the public that passengers were safe and all aircraft had been accounted for, while cautioning that restoring normal operations could take time.Mr Mullin said authorities were examining all possible causes of the telecommunications failure, including a potential connection with the planned introduction of a new artificial intelligence tool designed to assist air traffic controllers. He also confirmed that President Donald Trump has been briefed on the situation.The incident marks the second nationwide suspension of US flight departures since the terrorist attack on 11th of September in 2001.

. The Consulate General of India in Dubai commemorated Janjatiya Gaurav Divas with a special programme bringing together around 100 students from 20 CBSE schools across Dubai and the Northern Emirates of the UAE.The event paid tribute to the invaluable contributions of tribal communities to India’s history, freedom struggle and cultural heritage. As part of the commemoration, students participated in a speech competition, presenting the contributions of tribal freedom fighters through traditional attire and presentations.The programme also featured a hands-on workshop on Sohrai Art, a traditional tribal art form. It is a ritualistic wall-painting tradition practised by tribal communities in Jharkhand, typically created on mud walls by women during harvest and festive seasons.Six artists from UMSS Fine Arts and Fashion Academy, Abu Dhabi, under the banner of Kalashakthi, guided students through the workshop, offering them an opportunity to explore and appreciate India’s rich tribal artistic heritage.Janjatiya Gaurav Divas (Tribal Pride Day) is observed across India on 15th November every year to commemorate the birth anniversary of the tribal freedom fighter and anti-colonialist Bhagwan Birsa Munda and honour the contributions of tribal freedom fighters and communities to the country’s history and nation-building.The observance also seeks to preserve and promote tribal cultural heritage and recognise the role of tribal communities in India’s social and cultural development.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal, and Andaman and Nicobar Islands tomorrow.The Met Department has also predicted thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds over Kerala, Mahe and Lakshadweep during the next two days. Similar conditions are expected over Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, and Tripura tomorrow.Meanwhile, the weather agency has forecast mist and shallow fog at most places of Delhi during the morning hours tomorrow.The air quality in Delhi-NCR is in the ‘ Very Poor’ category. According to the Central Pollution Control Board, Delhi’s Air Quality Index was recorded at 303 as of 7 PM today.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has congratulated Anuj Shrivatri on becoming India’s 100th Chess Grandmaster, describing the achievement as a proud moment for the country. In a message on social media, the Prime Minister said India has reached a century in chess. He said the achievement reflects the immense talent, dedication and hard work of Indian chess players, as well as the growing popularity of the game among young people.The Prime Minister expressed hope that the milestone would inspire more youngsters to take up chess and strive for excellence. Anuj Shrivatri, who hails from Madhya Pradesh, achieved the milestone after winning the seventh ASEAN Plus Individual Open Chess Championship in the Philippines on Sunday. With this achievement, India has reached the landmark of 100 Grandmasters. Chess legend Viswanathan Anand became the country’s first Grandmaster in 1988.India has added five Grandmasters between July and November this year. Before Anuj Shrivatri, Ethan Vaz, Harshvardhan G B, S Ashwath and V Rathnavel had earned the prestigious title. India is also home to reigning World Chess Champion D. Gukesh, who is set to defend his world title later this month.

. World Diabetes Day is being observed today to raise awareness about the importance of early diagnosis, timely intervention and equitable access to quality healthcare. The theme this year, “Early Action on Diabetes”, highlights the need for comprehensive healthcare and age-appropriate treatment at every stage of life. The observance also underscores the importance of collective efforts to address the growing burden of diabetes worldwide.Health experts stress that early detection is essential to ensure that people living with diabetes receive the necessary treatment, care and support to manage the condition and lead healthy lives. Common warning signs of diabetes include increased thirst, frequent urination, persistent tiredness and blurred vision.Recognising these symptoms and seeking timely medical advice can help prevent delays in diagnosis and treatment. While Type 1 diabetes often develops rapidly, Type 2 diabetes usually progresses gradually and may remain undiagnosed for years because its symptoms can be mild or absent. Although Type 1 diabetes cannot currently be prevented, it can be effectively managed through appropriate treatment and continuous medical care. The risk of developing Type 2 diabetes can be reduced through regular physical activity, a balanced diet and a healthy lifestyle. For people already diagnosed with diabetes, timely medication, regular blood glucose monitoring and necessary lifestyle changes are essential to managing the condition and preventing serious complications.The World Health Organization has identified closing the gap in diabetes diagnosis as a global health priority. It has set a target, supported by its Member States, to ensure that at least 80 per cent of people living with diabetes are diagnosed by 2030.

. India concluded a historic campaign at the 2026 Summer Youth Olympics in Dakar, Senegal. It won 10 medals, including 2 Gold, 3 Silver and 5 Bronze. The medalists included 5 Khelo India Athletes.Of the 11 sports India competed in, the athletes won medals in 7 disciplines, including first-time medals in Swimming, Beach Wrestling and Wushu. India also won its first-ever gold medals in boxing at the Youth Olympic Games.India’s 10-medal tally at Dakar marks its second-best performance, surpassed only by the 13 medals won at the 2018 Youth Olympics. Khelo India Athletes Gunjan and Lairenlakpam Meetei won India’s first boxing golds, Shourya Ambure won the first athletics medal, and Taniya won the first youth wrestling medal.

. In Mizoram, three-day Leitlangpui Music Festival is underway in south Mizoram’s Lunglei town, bringing together established musicians, emerging bands and local entrepreneurs to showcase the state’s musical heritage and promote tourism. Organised by the Ministry of Tourism and Mizoram Tourism department, the festival began yesterday at Lena Stadium at Serkawn under the theme “Music Comes Home to Serkawn”. The festival seeks to connect that legacy with contemporary musicians and emerging talent.Addressing the inaugural ceremony, Tourism Minister Lalnghinglova Hmar said music was an inseparable part of Mizoram’s cultural identity and Serkawn held a special place in the state’s musical history. The minister said that the government aimed to take Mizoram’s music and cultural heritage to national and international audiences while creating opportunities for young artists, entrepreneurs and local communities. The festival features performances by established and emerging Mizo musicians.The second day includes a band competition with 10 finalists from Aizawl, Lunglei, Nagaland and Assam, while winners of the previous two editions, Swordtune and Knot, are also scheduled to perform. The final day will feature performances by several Mizo artists and bands, followed by the minister’s address and a fireworks display.

. Global crude oil prices displayed a mixed trend today. Brent crude was trading 0.3 per cent up at 96 US dollars and 12 cents per barrel. West Texas Intermediate crude was trading 0.1 per cent down at 87 US dollars and 61 cents per barrel, when reports last came in.

. Three crude bombs exploded at two court premises in Jashore district of Bangladesh on Thursday night, triggering panic among local residents and commuters. No casualties were reported.According to police and eyewitnesses, two crude bombs were hurled at the boundary wall of the Jashore District Judge’s Court, opposite the Jashore Press Club.Shortly afterwards, another bomb exploded inside the premises of the Chief Judicial Magistrate’s Court. The loud explosions caused panic in the area, temporarily disrupting traffic and pedestrian movement.Police visited the sites and collected fragments of suspected crude bombs, including pieces of tobacco tins believed to have been used in their construction.Police said unidentified assailants carried out the explosions before fleeing the scene. Police have launched an investigation into the incident.

. The Department of Pension and Pensioners’ Welfare will conduct the month-long fifth nation-wide Digital Life Certificate (DLC) campaign across the country from the 1st of next month. Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions Ministry said that this is the biggest-ever DLC Campaign undertaken by the Ministry. Electronics and Information Technology Ministry and UIDAI will provide technical support during this campaign. The Ministry said that the initiative will be adopted with a Whole of Government approach with the objective of reaching pensioners in the remotest corners of the country with focus on Face Authentication Technology. The Ministry said that face Authentication for Digital Life Certificate is a seamless and fast mode for DLC generation which can be used both on Android and Apple devices, making it easy and convenient for elderly Pensioners.The Campaign will be conducted in an Utsav mode by offering a bouquet of services such as Health Check-ups and Aadhaar updation for pensioners. Doorstep services to be provided to pensioners based on their requirement.

. Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has said, India recorded an all-time high in exports, reaching nearly 90 billion dollars in October this year.Addressing the inaugural ceremony of the India International Trade Fair (IITF) in New Delhi yesterday, Mr Goyal said the export figure of October comprised around 50 billion dollars in merchandise exports and 40 billion dollars in services exports. He further informed that India’s cumulative exports during the first seven months of the current financial year, up to October, has reached 570 billion dollars. Expressing confidence in the country’s export performance, the Minister said India is well on course to achieve its one-trillion-dollar export target this year.Mr Goyal also expressed confidence that India’s international trade will register growth of 15 to 16 per cent during the current year, despite ongoing conflicts and global uncertainties. He said the country’s performance reflects the resilience of its economy, the confidence of its exporters and India’s ability to overcome global challenges with determination and self-respect.Highlighting the strength of India’s domestic economy, Mr Goyal referred to the strong business activity witnessed during the recent festive season, particularly around Diwali. He said markets across the country recorded robust consumer demand and increased business activity. The Minister also pointed out that GST collections in October touched an all-time high for the month. He expressed confidence that November would also see record collections, reflecting the continued momentum of economic activity across the country. Referring to India’s long-term economic ambitions, Mr Goyal said the country, currently a four-trillion-dollar economy, aspires to become a 30-trillion-dollar economy by 2047.Speaking about the India International Trade Fair, the Minister said, the event has emerged as an important platform bringing together states, businesses, products and India’s diverse capabilities under one roof. He announced that the India Trade Promotion Organisation would take the IITF platform to international destinations by organising several overseas trade fairs, covering both specific sectors and multiple industries. These initiatives will provide Indian manufacturers, service providers and start-ups with opportunities to showcase their capabilities and connect with buyers and markets across the world, including developed economies. Mr Goyal added that the 45th edition of IITF had moved beyond incremental improvements, marking a significant step towards the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.The annual India International Trade Fair, organised by the India Trade Promotion Organisation, begins in New Delhi today. It brings together more than 3,500 exhibitors from India and abroad. The theme of this year’s fair is ‘Vikas aur Virasat’. A total of 32 States and Union Territories will participate in the 14-day event, showcasing their regional products, local industries, traditional crafts, cultural heritage, tourism potential and development initiatives. The fair will provide a major platform for businesses, entrepreneurs and participating states to promote their products, explore new opportunities and strengthen domestic as well as international trade ties.

Arunachal Pradesh’s Karateka Khyoda Talik has brought further recognition to the state by clinching a gold medal in the Male U21 Individual Kata category at the Commonwealth Karate Federation Club Championship 2026 held in Glasgow, Scotland.Congratulating the athlete on his achievement, Chief Minister Pema Khandu highlighted the growing presence of Arunachal’s sportspersons on the international stage.In a social media post, Khandu acknowledged the role of the Chief Minister’s Athlete Coaching and Empowerment Scheme (CM ACES) in nurturing young talents and providing them with opportunities and support to excel in competitive sports.

. Three major works of India’s literary and intellectual heritage including Kalhana’s Rajatarangini, the Mahabharata and Kautilya’s Arthashastra have been included in UNESCO’s Memory of the World Regional Register for Asia and the Pacific. The decision was taken at the 11th session of the register held in Jakarta, Indonesia. With this recognition, India’s total number of inscriptions in the regional register has risen to six. The three works represent different aspects of India’s knowledge traditions. Rajatarangini is a historical account of Kashmir, the Mahabharata explores Dharma, duty and human values, while Arthashastra deals with governance, diplomacy and statecraft. This recognition is a matter of pride for India’s civilisational continuity, its rich knowledge traditions and its contribution to the world. The development was announced by Member Secretary, Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA),  Dr. Sachchidanand Joshi which played an important role in preparing the nomination dossiers for all three works.

. Air India has issued a travel advisory warning of possible consequential disruptions to its flights to and from the United States. The advisory has been issued following a nationwide ground stop across US airports due to communication outages affecting air traffic operations.The airline has advised passengers to check the latest flight status on its official website and plan their journey to the airport accordingly. Air India said, their teams are closely monitoring the situation and will share the further updates.

The Embassy of India in Kathmandu today commemorated Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas, honouring the life and legacy of Bhagwan Birsa Munda.On the occasion, Embassy officials joined members of various indigenous communities of Nepal in paying floral tributes to Bhagwan Birsa Munda. The programme also featured a special lecture highlighting his life and legacy.The lecture further focused on the rich cultural heritage and traditions of indigenous communities in India and Nepal, bringing attention to the diverse cultural traditions of the two countries.The event brought together Embassy officials and members of Nepal’s indigenous communities to mark the occasion.

. Most Asian stock markets ended in negative territory today. Hong Kong’s Hang Seng shed 1.6 per cent, South Korea’s Kospi as well as Singapore’s Strait Times index lost nearly one per cent, China’s Shanghai Composite fell 0.6 per cent. In contrast, Japan’s Nikkei 225 gained over half a per cent and Taiwan’s Taiex rose 1.4 per cent.In European markets, London’s FTSE 100 rose 0.1 per cent, while Germany’s DAX eked out a marginal gain, when reports last came in.

. The Ministry of External Affairs has reiterated that the safety and well-being of Indian seafarers abroad remain a top priority for the government. Briefing media in New Delhi yesterday, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said an emergency travel certificate has been issued to Indian seafarer Akshay Harish from Keralam who was stranded at Chabahar Port in Iran, paving the way for his early return to India.The seafarer was left stranded in Iran after being informed that his passport and Continuous Discharge Certificate (CDC), essential documents for mariners, had been lost while he was aboard a merchant vessel. The MEA spokesperson said the Indian Embassy in Tehran and the Consulate in Bandar Abbas had reached out to him and were coordinating with the ship’s owner, agent and employer to complete the necessary documentation.With the emergency certificate now issued, the government is making all efforts, in coordination with his employer, to ensure his earliest possible return to his home state of Keralam.

. The Centre has extended the ban on the Islamic Research Foundation (IRF) led by fugitive preacher Dr Zakir Naik for another five years.In a notification issued yesterday, the Ministry of Home Affairs, declared IRF an unlawful association under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967, citing the organisation’s involvement in activities detrimental to the country’s security, communal harmony and secular fabric.In a social media post, the Office of Union Home Minister Amit Shah said, the decision reflected the government’s commitment to its policy of zero tolerance towards terrorism and anti-national activities. The post said, the organisation had been involved in activities aimed at inciting communal hatred, promoting terrorism and spreading separatist ideology.According to the Home Ministry notification, the government had first declared the Islamic Research Foundation an unlawful association in November, 2016. The ban was subsequently extended in November, 2021. The Ministry said, the IRF had been indulging in activities prejudicial to the security of the country, with the potential to disturb peace and communal harmony and disrupt the secular fabric of the country.The Ministry also cited speeches and statements made by the foundation’s founder and president, Dr Zakir Naik, saying they promoted enmity and hatred among different religious communities and inspired young people belonging to a particular religion, both in India and abroad, to commit terrorist acts. The notification further stated that the government considers it necessary to curb the organization’s activities to prevent the spread of anti-national sentiments.

. India’s forex reserves have recorded an increase of 2.49 billion to reach 719.547 billion dollars during the week ended 6th November 2026. According to an official press release issued by the Reserve Bank, the foreign currency assets, a major component of the reserves, spiked by 232 million dollars to 591.350  billion dollars.In the previous reporting week, the reserves had dropped by 2.691 billion dollars to 717.056 billion dollars.As per the statement, gold reserves jumped by 2.205 billion dollars to 104.796 billion dollars. The Special Drawing Rights – SDRs also went up by 52 million dollars to 18.610  billion dollars and India’s reserve position with the IMF also recorded a rise  of 1 million dollars to 4.791   billion dollars at the end of the reporting week.

. In the Indian bullion market today, 24 carat gold declined 1.4 per cent to 1,35,809 rupees per 10 grams. Meanwhile, silver shed 1.7 per cent to 1,78,000 rupees per kilogram according to the closing rates of the India Bullion and Jewellers Association.

. In Men’s ODI Cricket, India have entered the final of Under-19 Asia Cup beating Afghanistan by 8 wickets in the second semi-final match in Oman. Riding on impressive 93 runs scored by Captain Lakshya Rajesh Raichandani, India comfortably surpassed the target of of 228 runs scoring 230 for 2 in 36.5 overs.Earlier, opting to bat first, Afghanistan had posted 227 runs for the loss of eight wickets in their allotted 50 overs. India will face Pakistan in the final on Saturday.In the first semi-final today, Pakistan defeated Bangladesh by nine wickets to seal the place in the final.

He added that the life of Guru Gobind Singh, who gave his all to protect humanity, will continue to guide every generation for all eternity.

The third ODI in Hamilton was abandoned due to rain. New Zealand will aim to bounce back and register their first win in the series.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Andaman and Nicobar Islands today. The Met Department said that thunderstorm accompanied with lightning and gusty winds may prevail over Rajasthan. IMD has advised fishermen to avoid venturing into Andaman Sea and along and off Andaman and Nicobar Islands and Southeast Bay of Bengal till tomorrow.Meanwhile, air quality in Delhi-NCR is in the Very Poor category. . India’s merchandise exports rose by 45 per cent year-on-year to a record high of 49.47 billion US dollars in October this year despite the uncertainties in global markets. According to the data released by the Commerce and Industry Ministry, India’s total exports, including merchandise and services, surged by nearly 30 per cent year-on-year to reach 89.99 billion US dollars, while overall imports rose nearly 16.6 per cent to over 110 billion US dollars last month. Driven by a record merchandise export, the overall trade deficit narrowed to 20.09 billion US dollars.The Ministry noted that the major drivers of merchandise export growth in October included Petroleum Products, Electronic Goods, Gems and Jewellery, Organic and Inorganic Chemicals, and Engineering Goods. Meanwhile, India’s total exports, comprising merchandise and services, are estimated at over 568 billion dollars during April to October of the current financial year. This represents a growth of more than 16 per cent compared to the corresponding period of the previous financial year.

. Technology giant Microsoft has apologised for a major global service outage that disrupted millions of customers and business partners across several countries. The company has said that services are gradually recovering and stability is being restored across affected regions. In a social media post yesterday, Microsoft expressed regret over the disruption, acknowledging the trust customers place in its services and assuring them that the company takes its responsibility seriously.Microsoft clarified that the outage was caused by a technical issue and was not related to a cyberattack or artificial intelligence agents. According to the company, the disruption originated from a problem during an earlier network capacity upgrade, which surfaced following a subsequent network change. Microsoft said it had addressed the underlying technical issue and was working to restore services across all affected regions. The company also announced that it will release a detailed report on the incident after completing its investigation.The outage, which began on Thursday night, was linked to server health-check failures that made several affected servers unavailable. The disruption affected businesses, airlines and government operations across several countries, interrupting access to widely used Microsoft services, including Outlook, Teams and its artificial intelligence assistant Copilot.

. The NSE International Exchange (NSEIX), NSE’s global investment platform, has announced the expansion of its global investment offerings into seven key European markets through its GIFT City-based entity. The expansion increases Indian investors’ access to European-listed securities and Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs).NSEIX Global Access IFSC Limited (NSEIXGA), India’s first entity registered as a Global Access Provider under the regulatory framework of the International Financial Services Centres Authority, said in a statement that the expanded investment universe includes more than 11,500 securities, including over 8,200 UCITS ETFs across the European markets, including France, Germany, Ireland, Italy, the Netherlands, Switzerland and the United Kingdom.A key feature of the new offering is access to UCITS ETFs, which combine the benefits of exchange-traded investment products with an established European regulatory framework. These ETFs provide access to a wide range of global indices, markets, sectors, themes and asset classes, offering investors an alternative to investing in individual securities. UCITS ETFs also offer distinct tax advantages, further enhancing their appeal as an option for globally diversified investments.With this addition, investors will have access to a broader range of international investment products beyond the platform’s existing offerings in the US market. The expansion aims to cater to growing investor interest in international markets by providing access to a wider range of investment opportunities through a single integrated account.

. India’s Vivaan Kapoor settled for silver in the men’s trap event at the ISSF World Championships in Doha today. He also secured a quota place for the country for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. Vivaan was in superb form and looked set to become only the second Indian to win a world title in men’s trap after Manavjit Singh Sandhu, who triumphed at the 2006 World Championships in Zagreb, Croatia. However, Vivaan missed a clay bird in the shoot-off against Kuwait’s Abdulrahman Alfaihan, who clinched gold after both shooters had tied at 29 out of 30 in regulation.Vivaan became the third Indian shooter after men’s 10 metre air pistol marksman Jaypal Malviya and men’s 50 metre rifle 3-positions bronze medallist Niraj Kumar to secure an LA Olympic quota place.
